item: The test and Core-only jobs write a junit report and print their skips by class and test module (counts, never a reason) on red as well as green; portability and release.yml list their skips with -rsfE; a test pins every whole-suite line
summary: The skip block of a job (hundreds of lines under -rsfE) sits where the only log reader a session has never reaches: it returns about the last 13 KB, and on core-only that is the installed-versions block. 'What did this job not run' was therefore answered by re-running the suite locally (the 2026-10-29 audit counted 373). The test and core-only jobs now run pytest with --junitxml=$RUNNER_TEMP/junit.xml and, straight after the installed-versions step, scripts/ci_skip_summary.py reads the report (if: always(), continue-on-error, exit status 0 whatever it finds) and prints about 15 lines to the log and the step summary: tests, ran, skipped, expected failures; the skips by CLASS (import MODULE for an importorskip, otherwise other) and by TEST MODULE (largest 25 first, the rest summed in one line). It prints no reason: pytest keeps a skip's free text beside an absolute path (a collection-time skip carries ('/abs/path/test_x.py', 2, "Skipped: could not import 'duckdb': ...") as its element TEXT, its message being only 'collection skipped'), so every line is a fixed word, an integer or an identifier matched by a strict pattern before use, and the XML is parsed with defusedxml. The portability job (macOS per push, Windows weekly; no junit there, PowerShell does not expand $RUNNER_TEMP) and release.yml's test step, the two whole-suite lines still bare, now run -rsfE. tests/test_ci_pytest_flags_and_preflight.py now scans EVERY whole-suite pytest line of ci.yml and release.yml for -rsfE (a new bare one is named; the four there today are listed so a deleted line cannot make it pass on nothing), pins the summary step (once, exact, if: always(), continue-on-error, straight after the versions step, no 'pytest' in its command because tests/test_ci_installed_versions_step.py finds the last pytest step by that word) and preflight.sh's difference from the job (-rsfE and --junitxml, both named in its header), each with mutants. tests/test_ci_skip_summary.py plants a path, a secret, a line break and a workflow command in every field a reason can reach and reads every output line against a list of fixed shapes; it summarizes the report a real pytest writes, so a pytest release that moves the shape fails there; it feeds a truncated, an entity-expansion and a missing report and expects one line and exit 0; and two variants that print the reason are caught by the same line check. Stated limits: the first run of the new step is on this PR's own CI (its output was read here only from local runs); the Windows portability leg has no skip summary; the skips of jobs that name files (crypto, columnar, sqlcipher) are not summarized.
